candidates.title: The enemy courier delivers your amended attack order

layers.unit: An expedition in which planned relations change survival decisions.
Exploit a threat's exposed commitments while still surviving it.
Encounter issues card; hero intercepts; courier delivers or fails; boss executes normal warned attack.
A transported amended instruction controls one eligible future sweep only after delivery.

candidates.smallest_relational_unit: One physical courier, one amendable lane card and one future boss attack joined by a delivery commitment.
candidates.responsibility: Resolve whether a paid amendment reaches its carrier-dependent attack handoff; never invent a route, cancel danger or optimize hero behavior.
public_inputs: courier position, health and marked delivery route
public_outputs: ordinary boss windup with committed lane
rule_order: Issue at most one card for a designated next eligible sweep; store the ordinary lane as fallback and an eight-second delivery deadline.

At command admission, require a living carrier, proximity, pre-deadline unresolved card, unspent amendment and at least one seal. Reject invalid requests before cost; otherwise spend one seal and swap east/west once.
Resolve admitted movement, hits, damage and deaths under ordinary world rules. Carrier death before delivery marks the card failed; an admitted amendment is not refunded.

For a living carrier arriving no later than the deadline, deliver and freeze the card lane. Arrival is checked before same-boundary timeout. Timeout or route failure selects the recorded ordinary fallback.

At the next normal eligible sweep admission, take the delivered lane or fallback and issue the ordinary warning. This cannot rewrite an active attack. The usual hazard-reachability contract must admit, delay or relocate a new warning consistently.
Resolve the physical sweep normally, then retire the card. Delivery never prevents damage, changes XP budget or grants another seal.

finite_costs.mid_stage_refill: At most one seal from a paused optional cache choice; capped at two.
finite_costs.other_costs: interception recovery, preserving a hostile carrier and occupying an exposed route

candidates.failure_behavior: Killing or stalling the courier does not skip the boss attack: it restores the ordinary fallback with normal warning. Amendment expiry, carrier death and timeout retain spent cost. Hero death terminates the run without delivery reward or resurrection.
two_decisions: Preserve and escort the dangerous carrier to deliver an amended lane, versus kill it and face the unamended ordinary sweep.
Choose east to clear adds near a cache while accepting its crossing exposure, versus west to preserve a planned escape while leaving those adds alive.

manual_auto.manual: Approach, amend, withhold carrier-directed attacks and execute the warned escape; direct control still has spacing and recovery demands.
manual_auto.auto: Author intercept/amend, preserve-carrier target exclusion, fallback and ordinary sweep escape; normal path following may not invent delivery repairs.
required_policy_additions: near unresolved courier with seal reserve
exclude the named courier while amended card pending
manual_auto.editor_fit: Pending: the existing six-rule editor has not been shown to express both escort responsibility and recovery.

candidates.state_illustration: Seals 2 -> 1 on east-to-west amendment. Courier reaches the lectern at t=6 of deadline t=8: delivered west. Killing it at t=5 instead selects recorded east, with seals still 1. Both branches issue an ordinary sweep warning.
candidates.integration: Mason is the illustrative selected hero. Stage 1 has a legible delivery path; stage 2 adds a flanking threat so wall placement may help the courier or stall it; stage 3 pressures delivery timing near a boss phase change. A mid-stage seal refill competes with an ordinary defensive item. Other heroes retain ordinary combat and can decline the optional dispatch tool.
candidates.recomposition: Progression supplies the finite optional tool; world resolution supplies carrier motion/death; the delivery rule emits one attack request; encounter admission emits a normal warning; player/policy issues ordinary commands and observes the result. Deferred interfaces are named rather than hidden in a strategy manager.
candidates.meaning_destroying_split: Removing either physical carrier survival or delivery-dependent handoff leaves direct lane selection plus a timer. A card-data unit alone cannot carry the player's obligation to preserve an enemy.
candidates.evolution_boundary: Extend by one explicitly typed lane family or one courier class only after this handoff is understandable; defer arbitrary text orders, multi-carrier logistics and global enemy planning.
candidates.expiration: Rerun if deterministic courier routes cannot coexist with warned escapes, controller rules cannot preserve the carrier deliberately, or the matched direct-timer control yields the same useful decisions.

reserve.title: Your pursuer certifies the emergency exit
reserve.unusual_dependency: A pursuer's two observed turns become a transferable one-use permission both sides can consume.
reserve.retained_rule: Preserve public turn recording, carried certificate, installation and the competing first matching traversal; do not normalize to a hero-only key.
reserve.elimination_test: Compare ordinary two-turn movement lock and enemy-operated gate under matched travel/cost. Eliminate the extra certificate layer if transfer or enemy consumption never changes a viable choice.
reserve.status: preserved G0 reserve; not recursively developed in R1-PRE

candidates.title: Teach the boss your escape handwriting

layers.unit: Creative planning with demanding execution across an expedition.
Author an incoming threat's consequence and exploit its visible learned expectation.
Prepare a gesture; receive an eligible hit; route its displacement; expose actual endpoint; enemy commits coverage.
One bounded gesture reroutes hostile knockback while its resolved endpoint updates a two-event public memory.

candidates.smallest_relational_unit: One prepared two-segment displacement gesture joined to one eligible hostile hit and a visible endpoint-memory commitment.
candidates.responsibility: Replace only an admitted knockback's direction sequence, preserving its magnitude budget and hit cost, then record its actual endpoint for the enemy's next declared coverage phase.
public_inputs: eligible hostile hit and ordinary displacement magnitude
rule_order: Admit one two-segment gesture from drawing or equivalent segment selection. Each direction belongs to the disclosed direction set; fractions sum to one. Invalid geometry/input rejects before cost. Spend one charge, retain one pending gesture and a ten-second expiry; reject replacement while occupied.

Resolve an eligible accepted hostile hit normally, including prevention, guard break, HP loss and death. Rejected contact, poison, self/terrain damage and zero-knockback events do not consume the gesture.

If the hero survives an eligible nonzero knockback with a live prepared gesture, consume it and route the original displacement budget along its two segments, using current collisions. No extra distance, invulnerability or recovery reset is granted.

After displacement resolution, append the actual endpoint's named public zone, even when collision truncated the path. Keep the last two resolved gesture endpoints. An expired unused preparation spends its charge without memory update.

If both recorded zones match, the enemy's next eligible coverage phase commits to that zone with an ordinary visible windup and finite hold. This is a fixed disclosed response, not hidden inference. Updating memory cannot rewrite an already committed phase.

Resolve coverage, hazards and ordinary combat under the common world contract. New lethal warnings account for any already-committed compulsory displacement and current recovery; accepting a later optional hit can still create voluntary danger.

finite_costs.mid_stage_refill: One optional refill cache choice capped at capacity.
finite_costs.other_costs: preparation recovery, original hostile hit and commitment to authored turn sequence

candidates.failure_behavior: Illegal preparation rejects before spending. Expiry gives no refund. Collision truncates motion without compensating movement or damage; actual endpoint still teaches the enemy. Death ends the attempt. Ineligible attacks remain dangerous but neither fund memory nor consume the prepared gesture.
two_decisions: Accept an eligible knockback to traverse an authored bend, versus dodge and preserve the charge while using ordinary movement.
Repeat an endpoint to draw the enemy's next guard toward it, versus choose an unremembered endpoint to preserve that escape region.

manual_auto.manual: Draw or select the segments, control acceptance/guarding and exploit the declared guard relocation.
manual_auto.auto: Author the same gesture, eligible-contact condition, health reserve and next alternate route. No synthetic human drawing errors or hidden path optimizer.
new_public_observations: memory pair and committed coverage zone
required_policy_additions: pending gesture usable for a named eligible attack
last two endpoints match named zone
manual_auto.editor_fit: Pending: gesture preparation, deliberate contact, recovery and betrayal may exceed six tactical rules.

candidates.state_illustration: An admitted hit supplies distance 6. A gesture allocates east 4 then north 2. A wall after east 3 truncates at that actual zone, which is recorded. Two endpoints in zone E lead to a warned E guard; a later westward gesture does not retroactively move that locked guard.
candidates.integration: Bastion is the illustrative selected hero, with protection making some deliberate contact affordable. Stage 1 teaches a clear knockback category; stage 2 adds poison/ranged pressure that does not trigger it; stage 3 exposes the two-zone coverage response. A mid-stage gesture refill competes with cleanse or burst. Ordinary damage and warned escape remain available in each stage.
candidates.recomposition: Progression supplies finite gesture resources; input authoring emits a legal segment contract; world resolution provides the accepted hit/magnitude and actual endpoint; enemy memory emits one warned coverage request; manual/policy chooses the next actions. Prepared drawing does not own damage, safety or route optimization.
candidates.meaning_destroying_split: Remove hostile-hit magnitude/cost and it becomes a special dash. Remove endpoint exposure and it becomes steerable knockback without its coupled liability. A gesture or memory unit alone does not preserve the relationship.
candidates.evolution_boundary: Permit one new gesture family or endpoint-zone layout after the two-segment version is learnable. Defer continuous gesture interpretation, persistent opponent learning and generalized adaptive AI.
candidates.expiration: Rerun if knockback is too rare to matter, endpoint zones are unstable to understand, collision feedback hides the commitment, policy authors cannot intentionally teach/revise, or a directional-dodge control reproduces useful choices.

reserve.title: The boss learns your punctuation and your items must obey it
reserve.unusual_dependency: One learned rest in a four-slot phrase jointly sets a boss pause and the hero's selected-item eligibility.
reserve.retained_rule: Keep two completed teaching phrases, one pending learned cycle and the shared rest restriction; equivalent visual/tapping controls and rejected uncertain input remain required.
reserve.elimination_test: Compare independently selected boss pause and item timing lock at matched resources. Reject the shared grammar if it changes no viable authored plan or only delays every item without a useful choice.
reserve.status: preserved G0 reserve; not recursively developed in R1-PRE

candidates.title: Defeat the boss by making its attacks unaffordable

layers.unit: Survive three bosses through authored strategic choices.
Use an enemy benefit to reduce its remaining capacity to threaten.
Choose lane lease; induce attack commitment; survive empowered reach; exhaust entitlement; claim defeat seal.
An eligible charge spends a finite boss budget, with greater reach and greater expenditure if initiated in leased space.

candidates.smallest_relational_unit: One finite boss attack entitlement coupled to a player-selected lease lane and its empowered attack fee.
candidates.responsibility: Resolve the spatially conditional attack expenditure and its explicit defeated-state admission; never choose the lure or treat waiting as an automatic win.
public_inputs: current boss position and eligible charge
rule_order: Enter a disclosed boss phase with finite entitlement B=6 and direct hero damage to the boss disabled for this phase. Ordinary hero actions against adds remain available. Base attacks already spend entitlement, so no optional lease item is mandatory.

At command admission, spend one collateral to lease east or west for eight seconds. Permit one active lease and at most two collateral per phase; occupied/invalid requests reject before cost. No cancellation refund or reset extension.

When the boss normally locks an eligible charge, inspect its source position. A leased source lane gives the charge two extra reach units and fee 2; otherwise ordinary reach and fee 1. Spend min(B, fee) exactly once and freeze fee/reach at lock. Expiry does not undo that commitment.

Resolve the physical charge, hits, hazards and recovery normally. Misses and legal interruptions retain the spent entitlement; interruption enters its declared normal recovery. Hero death closes the run before any seal benefit.

Once B reaches zero and that final admitted attack's recovery completes, stop issuing new charges and open the public defeat seal. Existing adds and hazards continue. The hero must survive an ordinary interact recovery at the seal to claim it; interrupted interaction leaves the seal open without duplication.
Seal completion marks this boss defeated once and admits ordinary next-stage progression. It does not restore HP, refill leases, generate extra XP or erase outstanding hazards.

finite_costs.other_costs: lease slot/item opportunity, lure position, enlarged enemy reach and exposed seal interaction

candidates.failure_behavior: Invalid lease rejects before spending. A lease at an unvisited source lane may expire without accelerating expenditure. Empowered misses still spend fee; ordinary misses spend base fee. There is no negative-budget debt or new attack after exhaustion. Hero death is terminal even on the final token boundary.
two_decisions: Lease a source lane and lure longer-reach attacks to reduce the number of surviving commitments, versus keep ordinary reach and endure more attacks.
Spend scarce collateral on the cache-adjacent lane to finish sooner near acquisition, versus the safer far lane at the cost of travel and delayed access.

manual_auto.manual: Choose lease timing, lure the boss to a source lane, execute the longer-reach response and claim the seal.
manual_auto.auto: Author source-position approach, lease admission, explicit escape and seal interaction; no automatic lure solver or guaranteed budget exhaustion.
required_policy_additions: eligible boss source in named lane
budget zero and seal open -> named interaction route
manual_auto.editor_fit: Pending: the lure and final interaction must coexist with survival/recovery within the chosen editor budget.

candidates.state_illustration: B=6. East leased charge spends 2 -> B=4. West normal charge spends 1 -> 3. East leased charge spends 2 -> 1. West normal charge spends 1 -> 0. Four survived commitments open the seal after recovery; six ordinary ones would do so without leasing. This counts commitments, not demonstrated successful survival.
candidates.integration: Veil is the illustrative chosen hero, using mobility/poison against adds while boss phase damage is disabled. Stage 1 has simple source lanes; stage 2 mixes poison pressure with source-lane travel; stage 3 adds a declared longer-reach response without removing ordinary affordable charges. A mid-stage lease-tool/collateral offer competes with cleanse; baseline survival can exhaust the boss without acquiring it.
candidates.recomposition: Progression supplies optional collateral; spatial world state supplies source-lane facts; encounter admission freezes reach and fee; world resolution handles the committed charge; exhausted-state resolution emits one seal; ordinary player/policy interaction completes boss progression. No generic economy or hidden encounter director is required.
candidates.meaning_destroying_split: Remove spatially conditional fee and it becomes surviving a fixed attack count. Remove empowerment and paying collateral simply accelerates a clock. Neither budget accounting alone nor a buff alone carries the deliberate benefit-to-liability choice.
candidates.evolution_boundary: Extend only one named eligible attack family or lane layout after this phase is comprehensible. Defer monetary trading, persistent leasing, multi-boss markets and unlimited resource conversion.
candidates.expiration: Rerun if players cannot influence source position, lease choices are always dominant or useless, surviving a fixed attack count reproduces the plans, or the changed boss-resolution operation violates the user's intended boss outcome.

reserve.title: Help the boss shine so you can drag its shadow
reserve.unusual_dependency: A protecting lamp enlarges the boss's indirect manipulation surface, making assistance useful against it.
reserve.retained_rule: Keep protection gain, shadow endpoint, bounded hook displacement and three public cuff targets; do not normalize to a free grapple or an ordinary stun.
reserve.elimination_test: Compare fixed-size shadow handle and ordinary positioning hook at matched protection/cost. Remove the light-protection coupling if it produces no distinct useful manipulation choice.
